I'm not in favour of the this change, since this is a constant pattern, matching the template as defined in 802.1X-2020, 11.11.
I'm contemplating extracting all these into the main dissection function and passing it in as function parameter.

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/24085/diffs?diff_id=1726058590&start_sha=43023567938b57bc4d45639da9906984d4efec50#d4a837ac5ca66d8396a7cef3c7bcd4e0afcc2c3c_939_939)

Given the comment above, this should not matter, but extending a ti's length causes post dissection analysis tools (like MATE) to not have access to the data not covered by the original ti length. The pattern for unknown length ti's should be to have them extend to the end of the TVB, then reigned back in to their intended length.
I think I managed to improve this somewhat with 51e0dfa0057783b52d3b7e00cd4af1395b96b630 but there might still be some issues as you mention.

It should only add the proto_data for LATEST_KEY on the first visit - see the new line 978 - so we shouldn't need a test here too. Check me if I'm wrong

This is true. It works, though somewhat less efficient.

Btw: should we rename `tmp_value` to `pn_key` though, to match the name used in `dissect_sak_use()`?
